title: Logarithmic differential generators with finite characteristic cokernel
statement:
Let $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], log smooth in the chart sense of [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Fix a chart $Q\to N$ on $Y$, where $Q$ is fine saturated and $Q^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, set $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $B=M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$, and regard $A^\times$ as a subgroup of $B$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The relative logarithmic differential module $\omega_{f,\bar x}$ means the $A$-module generated by $da$ for $a\in A$ and $d\log m$ for $m\in M_{\bar x}$, subject to additivity and the Leibniz rule for $d$, $dc=0$ for elements $c$ from the geometric local ring of $Y$, $d\log(mm^{\prime})=d\log m+d\log m^{\prime}$, $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$, and $d\log f^\flat(b)=0$ for $b\in N_{f(\bar x)}$. Then $C=B/A^\times$ is a finitely generated torsion-free abelian group. There exist $r\geq0$, $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in M_{\bar x}$, and an integer $n\geq1$ invertible in $A$ such that $(d\log t_i)_{i=1}^r$ is an $A$-basis of $\omega_{f,\bar x}$ and the cokernel of
$$\mathbf Z^r\oplus Q^{\rm gp}\longrightarrow C,\qquad (a,q)\longmapsto\sum_i a_i[t_i]+[f^\flat(q)]$$
is finite and killed by $n$. Moreover $A^\times$ is $n$-divisible: every unit is the $n$th power of a unit. A basis here means that every vector has a unique linear expansion; $r=0$ and $n=1$ are allowed.

source.place: Expose XVI Proposition 3.6.3 proof, printed p.252, choice of t_i and characteristic-group cokernel; Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed pp.136--138, chart criterion. Read the cokernel modulo units, as in Lemma 3.6.4.

proof.text: Identify $A$ with the affine pointed-etale-neighbourhood ring colimit: geometric stalks are the colimit over all pointed neighbourhoods, and the affine-neighbourhood cofinality lemma permits restriction to the same affine diagram defining the strict henselization. The strict-henselization local-structure lemma makes $A$ a local strictly henselian ring. Write $\mathfrak m$ for its maximal ideal and $k=A/\mathfrak m$; in particular $k$ is separably closed.

source.place: Stacks Tag 04HX (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring); ILO XVI 3.6.3, p.252, geometric local ring

proof.text: Choose an fs chart $P$ for $M$ at $\bar x$, and put $F=\{p\in P:\alpha(p)\in A^\times\}$. Since a product in a local ring is a unit exactly when both factors are units, $F$ is a face. The chart pushout presentation identifies $M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}/A^\times$ with $P^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$. The face-sharpening lemma identifies this with the group completion of a sharp fs monoid and says that it is free abelian of finite rank. Thus $C=B/A^\times$ is finitely generated and torsion-free.

The differential relations show that the $d\log m$ span $\omega=\omega_{f,\bar x}$. Indeed, for $a\in A$, choose $\epsilon=0$ if $a$ is a unit and $\epsilon=1$ otherwise. Then $a+\epsilon$ is a unit and hence a section of the log structure, and $da=d(a+\epsilon)=(a+\epsilon)d\log(a+\epsilon)$. The finite-freeness input gives $\omega\simeq A^s$. Consequently finitely many of the spanning $d\log m$ generate it. Apply the selected-basis lemma with the split injection $\omega\simeq A^s$ and the prime $\mathfrak m$: it selects a subset of these generators that is a basis after localization at some $h\notin\mathfrak m$. Since $h$ is a unit, that localization is $A$ itself. Write this basis as $d\log t_1,\ldots,d\log t_r$, allowing the empty basis if $s=0$.

source.place: ILO XVI 3.6.3, p.252, choice of t_i; Stacks Tag 07C6 (smoothing.tex, lemma-find-strictly-standard), selected bases of split modules

proof.text: Put $D=C/\operatorname{im}(Q^{\rm gp})$. Define a $k$-linear map $k\otimes_A\omega\to k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}D$ by $1\otimes da\mapsto0$ and $1\otimes d\log m\mapsto1\otimes[m]$. All defining relations hold: base log sections and units have zero class in $D$, while if $m$ is not a unit then $\alpha(m)$ has zero residue, so the relation $d\alpha(m)=\alpha(m)d\log m$ also maps to zero. The map is surjective because the classes of monoid elements generate $D$. The basis from Step 3 therefore spans the target. Passing to $H=D/\langle[t_1],\ldots,[t_r]\rangle$, the tensor product $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}H$ is generated by images of those basis vectors, all zero; hence it vanishes. This is exactly the cokernel group in the statement after extending scalars to $k$.

source.place: ILO X Proposition 1.2 proof, pp.136--137, displayed surjection (1) and paragraph concerning k(x) tensor u; XVI 3.6.3, p.252

proof.text: The group $H$ is finitely generated as a quotient of $C$. Apply the finitely generated abelian group structure theorem. A free summand $\mathbf Z$ contributes a nonzero copy of $k$ to $k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}H$, so there is no free summand. A summand $\mathbf Z/q^e\mathbf Z$ with $e>0$ contributes $k/q^e k$: this is nonzero precisely when $q=\operatorname{char}k>0$. Thus $H$ is finite and its order $n$ is positive and prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ (with no restriction in characteristic zero). In particular multiplication by $n$ kills $H$, and the image of $n$ in $A$ is a unit because its residue is nonzero. For $H=0$ choose $n=1$.

source.place: ILO X Proposition 1.2 proof, p.137, cokernel killed by an integer invertible in k(x); XVI 3.6.3, p.252

proof.text: For any $u\in A^\times$, the polynomial $T^n-\bar u\in k[T]$ has derivative $nT^{n-1}$, which is nonzero at every root: its roots are nonzero and $n\neq0$ in $k$. Since $k$ is separably closed it has a root $a_0\in k^\times$. Apply the henselian local root-lifting criterion to the monic polynomial $T^n-u\in A[T]$ and this simple residue root. It gives $a\in A$ with $a^n=u$ and residue $a_0$, so $a$ is a unit. Thus $A^\times$ is $n$-divisible. The chosen $t_i$ and $n$ satisfy all assertions, including unique expansions by the definition of basis.

source.place: ILO XVI 3.6.3, p.252, units are n-divisible; Stacks Tag 04GG (algebra.tex, lemma-characterize-henselian), simple-root criterion

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-ea94560ad (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and all 11 cited statements in full, and checked them against the sources. Sources: ILO XVI Prop 3.6.3 proof and Lemma 3.6.4, pp.252-253, and ILO X Prop 1.2 proof, pp.136-137 (the surjection (1), the cokernel killed by m invertible, and O^* m-divisible). The item statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the version Q50 created. Its cokernel is read modulo units; the printed version into the full M^gp is false (identity of Spec k-bar with trivial logs). Steps: (1) The geometric stalk equals the affine strict-henselization colimit (cofinality lemma plus the def's independence of the representative subcategory), and the local-structure node makes it strictly henselian; only separable closedness of k is used. (2) A chart P gives F=beta^{-1}(A^x), a face; the pushout gives C=P^gp/F^gp, which face-sharpening makes free of finite rank. (3) da=(a+eps)dlog(a+eps), so the dlog m span omega. omega is finite free by the new node, and the selected-basis lemma at the maximal ideal (h a unit) picks a dlog basis. (4) The residue map k⊗omega -> k⊗D: I checked every relation (alpha(m) in the maximal ideal or m a unit; f^flat(b) lies in im Q^gp via the chart), it is surjective, so k⊗H=0. (5) By the structure theorem H has no free part and no char-k primary part, so n=|H| kills H and is invertible in A. (6) T^n-u is separable, has a root in k, and root-lifting gives n-divisibility of the units. Small cases tested: identity with trivial logs, log point, tame Kummer map (n=e), wild map excluded. New node local-freeness: this is Kato 3.10 at the stalk, and it is true for the chart-sense definition (O⊗C_i is free when the torsion order is invertible, and smooth c_i gives a split extension). It is strictly weaker than the item, so neither a restated clause nor circular, and it is self-contained with three kinds of search. No duplicate found in the DAG or the blueprint. The 5 declared tool uses are accepted as generic local-algebra and monoid tools. Batch-5 flags, checked by computing each closure directly: lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening reaches only face-localization, fg-torsion-free-free and two trf definitions; def-trf-fs-log-blowup is a general definition reaching only def-trf-log-regular-pair; def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale reaches only those definitions. None is a step of the trace formula or Poincare duality proofs, so all are accepted. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem EtaleLogHom.exists_logDifferential_generators {X Y : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}} (f : EtaleLogHom X Y) (hf : f.IsLogSmooth) {Q : Type u} [CommMonoid Q] (hQ : IsFineSaturatedMonoid Q) [IsMulTorsionFree (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup Q)] (β : Q →* Y.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y.scheme)))) (hβ : Y.logStructure.IsChart (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y.scheme)) β) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme) : Group.FG (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (X.logStructure.characteristic t)) ∧ IsMulTorsionFree (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (X.logStructure.characteristic t)) ∧ ∃ (r : ℕ) (ts : Fin r → X.logStructure.stalk t) (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n ∧ IsUnit (n : strictLocalRing X.scheme t) ∧ (∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (strictLocalRing X.scheme t) (f.LogDifferential t), ∀ i, b i = f.logDLog t (ts i)) ∧ Finite (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (X.logStructure.characteristic t) ⧸ f.differentialGeneratorImage t β ts) ∧ (∀ c : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (X.logStructure.characteristic t) ⧸ f.differentialGeneratorImage t β ts, c ^ n = 1) ∧ ∀ a : (strictLocalRing X.scheme t)ˣ, ∃ b : (strictLocalRing X.scheme t)ˣ, b ^ n = a
